question: Why does a solid where the Conduction Band is partially filled (or overlaps with the Valence Band) behave as a good conductor (Metal)?

options.A: Because the large energy gap prevents electron scattering.
options.B: Because electrons can easily move to nearby higher energy states within the same band under an electric field.
options.C: Because the valence band is completely full and rigid.
options.D: Because the density of nuclei is higher than in semiconductors.
